profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's original Midlothian, Texas data center campus, a 375-acre site in the Railport industrial park that the Dallas Morning News reported as a roughly $600 million project when it broke ground, Google's first data center in Texas and one of four the company was simultaneously building in the US at the time alongside facilities in Alabama, Virginia, and Tennessee. The Midlothian campus opened in 2019, and Google said it expected the completed facility to employ around 40 permanent staff, generating hundreds of construction jobs over the build-out; the city of Midlothian offered Google a 10-year tax abatement covering 100% of personal property taxes and 85% of improvement taxes to help attract the project, and Google contributed a $100,000 grant to Midlothian Independent School District for STEM programs. Google has continued expanding the site well past its original single building: on September 2, 2026, Google announced a $40 billion Texas investment through 2027 that includes a fourth Midlothian building backed by nearly $1 billion in additional spending, part of what the company has described as three AI-focused data center hubs across the state. Google's own Ellis County data center location page confirms the campus but, consistent with the company's general disclosure practice, does not publish individual building addresses, square footage, or MW power capacity; a roughly 86-megawatt figure some third-party data center trackers cite for the Midlothian campus has not been confirmed by Google directly and this registry declines to adopt it as fact. This building is one of at least three Google has built along V V Jones Road on the Midlothian campus.

Ercot, the grid operator for most of Texas, has flagged data center and large-load interconnection requests, heavily concentrated in North Texas corridors like Ellis County, as a major driver behind its 2026 long-term load forecasts, prompting new large-load interconnection study procedures the Public Utility Commission of Texas adopted to manage how quickly hyperscale campuses like Google's Midlothian and Red Oak sites can add capacity to the grid.

reading.body:
Google operates a data center campus in Midlothian, Ellis County, Texas, whose exact power capacity remains unpublished by Google itself. A third-party aggregator estimates the campus at approximately 86 megawatts of IT load, but this figure is unconfirmed and should be treated as a lead rather than operator specification. Google's disclosure policy limits public information to state-level investment figures, withholding individual facility addresses, square footage, and power consumption.

If the 86 megawatt estimate holds, the campus would represent a facility capable of hosting roughly 2,150 racks at standard 40 kilowatt-per-rack AI training density, or equivalent consolidations at higher power density. Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities in this registry, of which only 18 have published megawatt figures totaling 468 megawatts. At 86 megawatts, this campus would rank outside the top 18 published facilities in the state, though the population of unmeasured facilities suggests many others operate at unknown scale.

Google has announced a $40 billion expansion across three AI data center campuses in Texas, with filings indicating a fifth building planned at the Midlothian site according to public reporting. The actual trajectory of this campus depends on Google's build-out schedule and power supply constraints at the Midlothian location, neither of which are published. Without official capacity disclosure, this facility remains mapped but unquantified in assessments of Texas data center growth.
